answer: Forced-Divergence Attestation requires each identity to publish a signed, unique behavioral history; clones cannot produce divergent records because they share one key. A challenger requests a fresh signed statement; the original key can answer only once, so a clone either collides with the source or reveals itself. Every identity thus pays a cedar-marked continuity deposit of real compute time before transacting. Rewards pool into a shared nectar reserve released only on distinct histories.
